subject: geography
title: Drainage Basin: Stores Fill in Sequence, the River Lags Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: A student says the river peaks when the rain is heaviest, because rain runs straight off the surface into the river. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - the discharge peak always matches the rain peak

The basin stores fill in sequence - interception first, then the soil store, then groundwater - and overland flow only switches on once the soil saturates, so discharge peaks after the peak rain and then recedes slowly, sustained by groundwater baseflow.
The river never rises during a storm, because interception catches all the rain
The river peaks before the rain, because groundwater responds first

questions.misconception: The river peaks when the rain is heaviest, because rain runs straight off the surface into the river.
questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: The river peaks when the rain is heaviest, because rain runs straight off the surface into the river. Reteach point: The basin stores fill in sequence - interception first, then the soil store, then groundwater - and overland flow only switches on once the soil saturates, so discharge peaks after the peak rain and then recedes slowly, sustained by groundwater baseflow.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain why the channel and the hydrograph stay flat while the first store fills.
questions.answer: The interception store catches the first rain and only begins to spill once it is full, so almost no water reaches the channel while it fills.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names the interception store and the fill-before-spill rule: no spill, no flow to the channel.

questions.prompt: After the rain has gone, why does the river recede only slowly?

choices.text: Because overland flow keeps switching on and off
Because groundwater baseflow sustains the flow as the groundwater store drains slowly
Because the interception store refills and spills again
Because the soil store saturates a second time

questions.feedback: Scene 4 shows the recession sustained by groundwater baseflow: the store that filled last empties last, so the fall is slow.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state what must happen to the soil store before overland flow switches on.
questions.answer: The soil store must fill by infiltration until it saturates; only then does overland flow switch on and run over the surface to the channel.
questions.feedback: A strong answer pairs saturation with the switch: no saturation, no overland flow.
